subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should `sessions_spawn(runtime: "acp")` gain a core OpenClaw skill-context injection contract, and which selection, redaction, prompt-layer, audit, and resume semantics are allowed?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the change crosses ACP prompt context, session state, security boundaries, Codex/native skill behavior, and possible default config surfaces, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Design ACP contract first
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers specify selection modes, redaction/audit metadata, prompt layer, resume behavior, and native/Codex parity requirements before implementation.

options.title: Limit to explicit skill ids
options.body: Scope the first implementation to explicit `sessions_spawn` skill ids only and defer auto/default selection until observability and privacy behavior are proven.

options.title: Decline core injection
options.body: Keep ACP harnesses isolated from OpenClaw-rendered skill content and point users to harness-native skills, MCP bridges, or plugin workflows instead.

recommendation.title: Design ACP contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers specify selection modes, redaction/audit metadata, prompt layer, resume behavior, and native/Codex parity requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the ACP runtime/control-plane and `sessions_spawn(runtime: "acp")` surface that the decision would extend.
